title: Aster architecture snapshot
text: Project Aster is Northstar Systems' private retrieval service led by Mina Choi. The January build uses SQLite for durable metadata, the Orchid-2 embedding model, and a 30-minute query-cache TTL. Redis was evaluated but is not used in the deployed service. The default document chunk size is 768 tokens. Export bundles begin with the ASCII header ASTR1. These format details are compatibility constraints for internal tooling, although they are not expected to matter to most users.

title: Aster K-17 baseline benchmark
text: On benchmark set K-17, Aster's January baseline reports recall@10 of 0.72 and p95 query latency of 420 ms. The run used Orchid-2 and the default 768-token chunking configuration. Measurements were collected by the performance harness build perf-1.8. The report does not compare Aster with Northstar Research projects.

title: Astra program overview
text: Project Astra is a Northstar Research experimental graph-retrieval program led by Jin Park. Astra is separate from Northstar Systems' Project Aster despite the similar name. Astra focuses on graph-assisted association and does not share Aster's production datastore or release process. References to Astra should not be treated as aliases for Aster.

title: Aster memory and batching tuning memo
text: Aster remains on SQLite and Orchid-2 in the February tuning branch. Production containers have a 4 GB memory limit. The optional batch prefetch path is controlled by feature flag batch_prefetch and is disabled by default. The team rejected a full in-memory snapshot experiment because its peak memory exceeded the current container budget.

title: ASTR-1 telescope ingest schedule
text: The Observatory Group's ASTR-1 telescope pipeline will ingest calibration frames every 30 minutes during the February campaign. ASTR-1 is an astronomy instrument identifier and has no relationship to Northstar Systems' Aster software project, its ASTR1 export header, or Northstar Research's Astra program.

title: Astra graph retrieval benchmark
text: Astra's graph retrieval prototype recorded p95 latency of 310 ms and recall@10 of 0.79 on the NR-G9 evaluation set. The run used the Orchid-4 experimental encoder. These results are for Project Astra, not Project Aster, and should not be used as Aster production benchmarks.

title: Aster metadata store migration plan
text: Aster will migrate durable metadata from SQLite to PostgreSQL. The cutover is scheduled to become effective on 2026-03-05. SQLite remains the correct description of production before the cutover; PostgreSQL is the production store from the effective date onward. The migration does not change the ASTR1 export format.

title: Aster Orchid-3 rollout benchmark
text: Aster will make Orchid-3 the production embedding model on 2026-03-20, replacing Orchid-2 for new retrieval indexes. On K-17 with PostgreSQL, the rollout candidate measured recall@10 of 0.81 and p95 latency of 360 ms. Existing historical January benchmark reports should not be relabeled as Orchid-3 runs.

title: Aster cache freshness change
text: To reduce stale-result windows, Aster's query-cache TTL changes from 30 minutes to 10 minutes effective 2026-03-08. The 30-minute setting remains historically correct for earlier deployments. This change is independent of the Orchid-3 rollout and does not alter the document chunk size.

title: Erratum for January Aster latency benchmark
text: The January K-17 report contained a clock-calibration error in perf-1.8. The previously reported p95 latency of 420 ms was incorrect. Reprocessing the original trace with the corrected clock gives 450 ms. This is a correction of the January measurement, not a performance change that occurred in April. The January recall@10 value of 0.72 remains valid.

title: Partner validation of Aster build 3.2
text: BluePeak's validation of Aster build 3.2 on K-17 reports p95 query latency of 300 ms with PostgreSQL and Orchid-3. BluePeak states that it used the published K-17 procedure and production-equivalent hardware. The report does not explain why its latency differs from Northstar Systems' internal audit of the same build.

title: Internal audit of Aster build 3.2
text: The internal audit of Aster build 3.2 on K-17 reports p95 query latency of 335 ms with PostgreSQL and Orchid-3. The audit team reviewed BluePeak's 300 ms result but could not reconcile the difference before publication. Both reports refer to build 3.2 and claim the published K-17 procedure; no authoritative resolution is available yet.

title: Compaction strategy decision
text: The Aster architecture council selected delta compaction for the next index-maintenance cycle. The decision cites two constraints: production containers are limited to 4 GB, and the PostgreSQL-backed metadata path introduced in March supports the delta bookkeeping. A full-snapshot design was rejected after a prototype peaked above 5.5 GB. The decision record makes no claim that delta compaction improves recall quality.

title: Cache incident review
text: A stale-search incident lasted eight minutes before a refreshed result became visible. The review notes that the current Aster cache TTL is 10 minutes, so the observed delay is consistent with the configured upper bound. The incident did not involve a return to the former 30-minute TTL and did not change the cache policy.

title: Nova integration requirements for Aster
text: Project Nova will consume Aster's retrieval API. Nova's launch checklist requires Aster deployments to use PostgreSQL and Orchid-3; environments still on SQLite or Orchid-2 are unsupported for Nova. The checklist also requires the ASTR1 export header for offline interchange. Nova does not depend on Northstar Research's Astra project.

title: Aster public rename to Aurora
text: Effective 2026-06-01, Project Aster's public product name is Aurora. Aster remains a valid internal and historical alias, and existing technical documents do not need to be rewritten as though Aurora had always been the name. The rename changes naming only; PostgreSQL, Orchid-3, the 10-minute cache TTL, and the ASTR1 export header remain unchanged.

title: Aurora component boundary update
text: The former monolithic Aster/Aurora architecture is now documented as two maintained components: Aurora Retrieval and Aurora Ingest. Retrieval owns query execution, cache behavior, and embedding-model use. Ingest owns document parsing, 768-token default chunking, and ASTR1 export generation. This is an organizational split of one product lineage, not the creation of unrelated projects.

title: Aurora export compatibility security note
text: Security review confirms that the Aurora Ingest export format is still the format inherited from Aster. Existing consumers should continue validating the ASTR1 header before processing bundles. The review does not alter the 768-token default chunk size and introduces no new benchmark claims. Documents that refer to Aster's export format remain historically meaningful after the Aurora rename.
